text:
Sam: Heads up — found a tiny poinsettia wilting on the 3rd-floor kitchen counter after yesterday's cookie swap. Left it on the windowsill with a note. Anyone know if this one survives office life? :poinsettia:
Priya: Oh no, poor plant! Thanks for rescuing it, Sam. You’re the plant whisperer :heart_eyes:
Jamie: 2nded, heroic move. If it’s droopy, maybe it just needs a little bottom-watering and more light. I can bring a small saucer later.
Sam: Good call. I gave it a little water but not sure about the soil. Note said "Please don't forget me" lol.
Nora: @Sam amazing. If anyone's taking holiday plants home, I can take it for the weekend to nurse it back. My windowsill is like a greenhouse :seedling:
Leo: I can help too — I have a small plant mister and some spare potting mix in my desk :handshake:
Priya: Team rescue! Want to do a mini handoff chain so it doesn’t get stranded during the holiday break? Maybe a quick sign-up here.
Sam: Yes please. Who can pick it up before EOD? Nora offered weekend care, Leo can do Wednesday handoff.
Nora: I’ll take it Friday evening and bring it back Monday next week unless someone claims it for home adoption :smile:
Jamie: If it’s still fragile after a week, adopt-to-home is probably safer during the break.
Sam: Cool. I’ll tape a little sticky with watering notes and tag the current caretaker. Ops-bot can we add a tiny reminder to #random on Friday: "Plant handoff at 5pm"? :robot_face:
ops-bot: Scheduled reminder set for Fri 17:00 in #random — "Poinsettia handoff & holiday plant hugs" :white_check_mark:
Leo: Also holiday update: leaving a couple of extra mugs and tea bags in the kitchen for anyone working late next week. Help yourselves :) :mug:
Nora: And if you grabbed a plant for your apartment, send pics! Plant adoption albums are my favorite :camera_with_flash:
Priya: Happy almost-holidays, team. Thanks for rescuing the poinsettia and the teamwork energy. :santa: :sparkles:
Sam: Agreed — thanks y’all. Happy holidays and plant-friendly vibes!
